Sorry Joe - here it is:

(with this clunky use of Switch statements, i can plot, but is there a better way to handle this as i anticipate dozens of separate ts datasets? Thanks in advance!)

server.R
*****************************************************

library(shiny)
library(forecast)

inp <- read.csv("C:/../aggregate-ts-1wt-2wt-mc1v-jul07-nov012.csv")
all1wt <- ts(inp$WT1, freq=12, start=c(2007,7))
all2wt <- ts(inp$WT2, freq=12, start=c(2007,7))
allMc1v <- ts(inp$MC1V, freq=12, start=c(2007,7))
allProd <- ts(inp$AllWTProducts, freq=12, start=c(2007,7))

# Define server logic required to plot various commodities
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

datasetInput <- reactive(function() {
    switch(input$dataset,
           wts1 = all1wt,
           wts2 = all2wt,
           allPs = allProd)
  })
  # display selected commodity names
  output$commSelected <- reactive(function() {
    paste("Commodity selected is:", input$dataset, "for", input$range, "months")
  })

 # Generate a time series table of the requested commodity and only 
  # include decomposition chart if requested
  output$CommodityTable <- reactivePrint(function() {
   switch (input$dataset, 
wts1 = all1wt,
wts2 = all2wt,
allPs = allProd)
  })
  
  # Generate a time series forecast plot of the requested commodity and only 
  # include decomposition chart if requested
 output$CommodityPlot <- reactivePlot(function() {
 switch (input$dataset, 
wts1 = plot(all1wt), 
wts2 = plot(all2wt),
allPs = plot(allProd))
 })

})
********************************************************************
ui.R
********************************************************************

library(shiny)

# Define UI 
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("Forecasting App"),

  # Sidebar with controls to select the commodity
  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("dataset", "Commodity:",
                list("1WT" = "wts1", 
                     "2WT" = "wts2", 
                     "All" = "allPs")),
 
    sliderInput("range", "Range in months:", 
                min=0, max=100, value=24),

    checkboxInput("decompose", "Decompose?", TRUE)
  ),

    # Show the caption and plot of the requested variable
  mainPanel(
    h3(textOutput("commSelected")),
    verbatimTextOutput("CommodityTable"),
    plotOutput("CommodityPlot")
  )
))

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: reading timeseries datasets into shiny
parts:
It's not related to why the plot isn't rendering, but you could replace the switch statement with an environment and get():

dataEnv <- new.env()
dataEnv$all1wt <- ts(...)
dataEnv$all2wt <- ts(...)
# etc.

datasetInput <- reactive(function() {
  get(input$dataset, pos=dataEnv)
})

Everywhere else, just refer to datasetInput()--you don't need to repeat the switch statement (or if you replace it with get(), the get() statement).

This seems like it should work though. The first thing I would do is make a non-Shiny R script to test plotting these different variables and make sure your R code is even correct. Then you can add print() statements (or browser() calls if you're familiar with R debugging tools) to your reactive functions to see when things are executing and what values they're producing.
